ToolHeader.title: Latin-Cyrillic Converter
ToolHeader.description: Convert Uzbek text between the Latin and Cyrillic alphabets, or into the new alphabet (ş, ç, ğ, ö). Your text never leaves the browser.

notes.e: Э at the start of a word, Е inside it

notes.ts: Ц only in loanwords: informatsiya → информация. In words like “ketsin” it stays т + с

howToUse.question: How do I use the converter?
howToUse.answer: Paste your text into the left panel — the result appears on the right immediately, with no button to press. The direction is detected automatically; switch from “Auto” to a fixed direction whenever you need to.

newAlphabet.question: Can I convert text to the new alphabet (ş, ç, ğ, ö)?
newAlphabet.answer: Yes. Pick “New Latin” above: Latin or Cyrillic text is converted into the alphabet that takes effect on 22 April 2027 — sh → ş, ch → ç, g' → ğ, o' → ö. “Latin” turns new-alphabet text back into the 1995 Latin alphabet. “Auto” only switches between Latin and Cyrillic: the new alphabet is always your choice.

isFree.question: Is it free? Do I need an account?
isFree.answer: It is completely free, with no account and no limits.

accuracy.question: How accurate is the conversion?
accuracy.answer: The converter handles the hard parts of Uzbek orthography: the sh + ch boundary (ishchi → ишчи), the tutuq mark (san'at → санъат), the -tsiya suffix (informatsiya → информация) and word-initial e → э. Links, email addresses, code and technical terms are left untouched. Even so, it is worth checking rare foreign names by eye.

files.question: Can I convert a Word or PDF file?
files.answer: Yes — Word (DOCX), PDF and TXT. Drop the file anywhere on the page or use the File button, then download the result as Word (DOCX) or TXT. Files up to 10 MB.

privacy.question: Where does my text go?
privacy.answer: Nowhere. The whole conversion runs in your browser — neither the text you type nor the file you upload is sent to a server.

difference.question: Why are some words left unconverted?
difference.answer: Links, email addresses, file names, code snippets and product names such as React or GitHub are preserved on purpose — they lose their meaning when written in Cyrillic.
